floor_history.headline: Floor 194 (no C body on HEAD) -> 101: de-cheated the retired chassis, fixed both flagged declarations to arrays, and sized IconC70 to 0x20; residual is a 5-seat callee-saved rotation plus one extra re

Floor held at 101; quantified the loop.c gate that costs the 7th callee-saved register (threshold bracketed 26..29, insn 312 savings 1 lifetime 2) and PROVED that killing that hoist alone restores tar

Floor 101 -> 99 and build_insns 193 -> 194 (= target's 194): declaring D_800A3590 as an array of a 2-byte record routes the read through expand_expr's COMPONENT_REF/get_inner_reference offset path, wh

frontier.hypothesis: Stopping loop.c strength_reduce from reducing the D_800A3590 address giv removes the fourth induction register, which is the entire 0x88-versus-0x80 frame delta and the base the five-seat callee-saved rotation sits on.
frontier.mechanism: loop.c:3824 `v->lifetime * threshold * benefit < insn_count` with threshold 28..31 (loop.c:3241), insn_count 48 and lifetime 1 leaves exactly two terms C can move. (a) `bl->biv_count` for biv 75 (var_s0): at biv_count 2 the combined benefit falls from 4 to 2 and at biv_count 3 to 0, and biv_count counts the induction INCREMENT insns recorded for that biv register. (b) `benefit` itself, which general_induction_var fixes at 4 for a mult-2 DEST_ADDR giv (2 per rtx operation) -- only a scale-1 access earns the benefit-2 rejection that D_800A3560 already enjoys.
frontier.next_probe: (a) Check whether any byte-faithful source shape gives var_s0 more than one increment site -- the two arms of the `code != 5 && code != 16` test are the obvious place, and duplicated-statement-into-arms is a sanctioned family if a plain form does not do it -- but FIRST read whether the target's single `addiu $s0,$s0,1` at 80070EC8 is even compatible with two source increments. (b) Ask whether the target's object model makes this access scale-1 rather than scale-2: D_800A3560 is a 3-byte-stride record array indexed by var_s0*3 in the same loop, so test whether D_800A3590's halfword is really a member of a parallel record whose stride the compiler sees as 1 element. Do NOT re-try the insn_count route -- it needs a loop 15+ RTL insns larger than ours and the target's is smaller.

frontier.hypothesis: D_800A3590's real record type is recoverable from its other consumers, replacing the codegen-motivated `struct RecC70 { s16 v; }` that currently blocks submission.
frontier.mechanism: The 2-byte stride is proven by the target's own addressing, but a one-member struct (and the equally contrived `extern s16 D_800A3590[][1];`, which measures the same 99) is a spelling of that stride, not evidence for it. The symbol's other consumers write and read the fields this function leaves alone, and their asm names the real offsets and widths -- the same method that resolved D_800A3560's array shape in s1.
frontier.next_probe: Read the `%hi/%lo(D_800A3590)` and base-register accesses in func_8006F100, func_80070188 and func_80070F78 (all still INCLUDE_ASM) and the declaration at src/text1b_b.c:271, build the true field list, and re-measure with the real type in place. Keep the census row's `alias of g_replay_motion_shared_state_d+6` suffix per the brief's DATA MODEL block (prong (c) amendment 2026-09-03). If the consumers show a bare halfword array with no record structure, emit a ruling-request naming the family before any submission rather than shipping the one-member struct.

frontier.hypothesis: IconC70's real tail layout (bytes 0x8..0x20) is recoverable from func_80069898's other callers, replacing the `s16 sp50[12]` placeholder that also blocks submission.
frontier.mechanism: The 0x20 size is proven by s1's frame arithmetic (target frame 0x80 = 0x18 outgoing args + 0x50 locals + 0x18 six callee-saved slots, with prim at 0x18 and icon at 0x48), but candidate.c spells the tail as a placeholder rather than as evidence. func_80069898 itself reads only offsets 0x0/0x2/0x4/0x6 of its $a1 argument, so the tail is written by its other callers.
frontier.next_probe: Read the $a1-relative stores in func_8006B120, func_8006CFBC, func_800720FC, func_80074488 and func_8006F97C, build the true field list, replace the placeholder, re-measure, and propagate the corrected type to the func_8006F97C and func_800720FC ledgers -- both are active queue siblings in the same TU. Carried unchanged from s1 and s2; untouched in s3.
